sections.html:
The bill comes from Orange County, not the city. Orlando sets its own rate, but the county Property Appraiser decides what your home is worth and the county Tax Collector mails one combined statement and collects the money. The city says it keeps about 35 cents of every property tax dollar. The rest is divided among Orange County, Orange County Public Schools, the St. Johns water management district and the library system.

In practice, anything that touches the bill goes to a county office. The city handles services, permits and its budget.

  • Orange County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, mailing address
  • Orange County Tax Collector: bills, payments, delinquent taxes, certificates
  • City of Orlando: its own millage rate and budget

Orlando's own rate is 0.00665, or 6.65 mills, and the city says it has stayed there for more than a decade. A mill is a tenth of a cent for each dollar of taxable value. That is only one line on your statement. County, school and water district levies add to it, and special assessments come on top.

The Property Appraiser posts the final millage for every taxing body by year. For a specific address, ask the Tax Collector for the bill itself, since the lines differ by neighborhood and by special taxing district.

Orlando has about 333,888 residents, up 8.4 percent from the 2020 count, and 131,179 households. Only about four in ten households own their home, and the middle owner-occupied value is $394,100. Roughly six in ten residents rent. For a seller, that means investors are a large part of the buyer pool for a house here, and a tenant may already be living in the property.

Show an investor or any other buyer the Tax Collector's account page and your exemption status up front. Mention any special district lines on the bill so they do not turn up as a surprise in the buyer's review period.

sections.h2: Due dates, discounts and late charges
sections.html:
Statements go out by the start of November. The gross amount is due March 31. Pay early and you get a discount that begins at 4 percent in November and drops each month to 1 percent in February. Whatever is still unpaid on April 1 is late.

Orange County payment schedule
Pay duringResult
November4 percent discount
February1 percent discount
By March 31Gross amount, no discount
April 1 onwardDelinquent, 3 percent minimum charge plus advertising cost
By June 1Certificate auction, bids opening at 18 percent

The office counts the day the money arrives, so a letter mailed on March 31 and delivered April 3 is late. If a lender escrows your taxes, the lender may receive the bill and you may get only a copy, so confirm the payment actually went out.

File a petition within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, which the Property Appraiser mails in August. The petition, one of the DR-486 forms, goes to the clerk of the court.

A denied exemption runs on a separate clock. A petition to the value adjustment board is due 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. Taxing bodies hold public hearings in September and October, and final statements arrive in November.

  • Read the August notice the week it arrives.
  • Count the 25 days from the mailing date printed on it.
  • Call the Property Appraiser first, because many errors get fixed informally.

Keep the notice in your sale file. It tells a buyer what the county proposes before final rates are set.

sections.h2: Homestead, Save Our Homes and portability
sections.html:
Homestead removes up to $50,000 from taxable value. Save Our Homes separately limits yearly growth in a homestead's assessed value to the smaller of 3 percent or inflation. The state's chart shows a cap of 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024.

The protection ends when you sell. The new owner is assessed at full just value the following January, so a buyer's first bill can be far above yours. If you plan to stay in Florida, portability can carry part of your savings to the next home. File it with the exemption application by March 1, and within three years of leaving the old homestead.

Get a written payoff from the county Tax Collector, and plan on any late balance being paid from your proceeds at closing. If you ever used the homestead tax deferral, ask the Tax Collector how a deferred balance is repaid when the house sells.

  • Check whether a tax certificate was sold against the parcel.
  • After April 1, pay with certified or cashier's funds, a money order or cash in person.
  • If a certificate has gone unredeemed for two years, act right away, since a tax deed application can follow.
  • Confirm your lender's escrow account has paid the current year.

A cash buyer skips lender underwriting and can often close quickly even when a tax lien sits on the parcel. Weigh that against listing costs and repairs before you choose a route.

sections.h2: A simple checklist before you list
sections.html:
Order matters here, so work through these in sequence. First, search the parcel on the Property Appraiser's site and confirm the owner names and exemptions are correct. Second, pull the Tax Collector's account page and note which years are paid. Third, request the payoff letter if anything is open. Fourth, gather your latest statement and the August notice for the buyer or title agent.

Finally, tell your closing agent how you want the current year divided with the buyer. Bills go out in November while closings happen all year, so the contract should say who owes what for the months each side owned the home.

faqs.q: Does Orlando collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Orange County Tax Collector sends one bill that includes the city's levy. Orlando sets its own millage rate and keeps about 35 cents of each dollar.

faqs.q: What is the city millage rate in Orlando?
faqs.a: The city's rate is 0.00665, or 6.65 mills, and it has held for more than ten years. Your bill also carries county, school and district levies.

faqs.q: When do Orlando property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. The full amount is due by March 31, and payment must reach the Tax Collector by then. A 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost follow.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap carry over when I sell in Orlando?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets assessed value to just value the next January 1. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, filed by March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I check my tax bill before listing a house in Orlando?
faqs.a: Search the Orange County Tax Collector's records by owner name, parcel ID or address. The Property Appraiser's parcel record shows value and exemptions.
